title: Rhai
subtitle: Evaluate expressions and rules stored as text
intro: Run Rhai expressions inside a query, pass row values as JSON context, and read a typed success or error result. Useful for configurable business rules, small transformations, and scripts that need local variables or branching.

reference.name: evalexpr_rhai(script)
reference.description: Evaluate a script without row context.

reference.name: evalexpr_rhai(script, context)
reference.description: Expose a JSON object as context inside the script.

reference.name: .ok
reference.description: JSON result on success; NULL when the script fails.

reference.name: .error
reference.description: Error text on failure; NULL when the script succeeds.

reference.name: context.field
reference.description: Read a field supplied by the SQL query.

reference.name: let / if / fn
reference.description: Bind variables, branch, and define helpers inside scripts.

notes.title: Keep the boundary explicit
notes.body: The result is UNION(ok JSON, error VARCHAR). Cast .ok to a SQL type before arithmetic or joins. Inspect .error to distinguish a failed script from a successful JSON null.

notes.title: Use it where rules change
notes.body: Scripts run per row. Keep routine transformations in native SQL; use Rhai when stored rules or branching improve clarity. A constant script can reuse its parsed expression while context changes.

examples.title: Evaluate and cast
examples.caption: Define helpers in the script; return its final expression.

examples.title: Apply one rule to each row
examples.caption: Use a constant rule with a different JSON context for each row.

examples.title: Read a failure without losing the query
examples.caption: A failing Rhai expression returns the error arm.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN evalexpr_rhai('fn sq(x) { x * x } sq(context.n)', {'n':7}).ok::INTEGER = 49 AND evalexpr_rhai('1 / 0').ok IS NULL AND evalexpr_rhai('1 / 0').error IS NOT NULL THEN true ELSE error('Rhai result/error contract failed') END;
